import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Sendov's conjecture

*Reference:* [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sendov%27s_conjecture)

Tags: Sendov Conjecture, Ilieff's Conjecture.

-/

open Polynomial

namespace Sendov

open Sendov

/-- The predicate that a polynomial satisfies the hypotheses of Sendov's conjecture.

`f.IsSendov` holds if `f` has degree at least 2 and all roots of `f` lie in the unit disc
of the complex plane. -/
def Polynomial.IsSendov (f : ℂ[X]) : Prop :=
  2 ≤ f.natDegree ∧ (f.rootSet ℂ ⊆ Metric.closedBall 0 1)

/-- `SatisfiesSendovConjecture n` states that Sendov's conjecture is true for every polynomial of
degree `n`. -/
def Nat.SatisfiesSendovConjecture (n : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ (f : ℂ[X]), f.IsSendov → f.natDegree = n →
    ∀ z, z ∈ f.rootSet ℂ → Metric.infDist z (f.derivative.rootSet ℂ) ≤ 1

/-- **Sendov's conjecture** states that for a polynomial
$$f(z)=(z-r_{1})\cdots (z-r_{n}),\qquad (n\geq 2)$$
with all roots $r_1, ..., r_n$ inside the closed unit disk $|z| ≤ 1$, each of the $n$ roots is at a
distance no more than $1$ from at least one critical point. -/
@[category research open, AMS 12 30 52]
theorem sendov_conjecture (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) : n.SatisfiesSendovConjecture := by
  sorry

/-- **Sendov's conjecture** states that for a polynomial
$$f(z)=(z-r_{1})\cdots (z-r_{n}),\qquad (n\geq 2)$$
with all roots $r_1, ..., r_n$ inside the closed unit disk $|z| ≤ 1$, each of the $n$ roots is at a
distance no more than $1$ from at least one critical point.

It has been shown that Sendov's conjecture holds when the degree of $n$ is at most $9$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 12 30 52]
theorem sendov_conjecture.variants.le_nine (n : ℕ) (hn : n ∈ Set.Icc 2 9) :
    n.SatisfiesSendovConjecture := by
  sorry

/-- **Sendov's conjecture** states that for a polynomial
$$f(z)=(z-r_{1})\cdots (z-r_{n}),\qquad (n\geq 2)$$
with all roots $r_1, ..., r_n$ inside the closed unit disk $|z| ≤ 1$, each of the $n$ roots is at a
distance no more than $1$ from at least one critical point.

It has been shown that Sendov's conjecture holds for polynomials of sufficiently large degree.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 12 30 52]
theorem sendov_conjecture.variants.eventually_true :
    ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, n.SatisfiesSendovConjecture := by
  sorry

end Sendov

findings.description: The hypothesis `hn : n ∈ Set.Icc 2 9` includes degree 9, whereas the cited low-degree result covers only n < 9, i.e. degrees 2 through 8. Here `f.natDegree = n` makes n the actual polynomial degree, so this is not a reindexing. The docstring repeats the same incorrect upper bound. This finding concerns the transcription of the cited bounded-degree result, not whether degree 9 is now settled by the subsequent full proof.
findings.source_evidence: Wikipedia states: “The conjecture was previously proven for n < 9 by Brown and Xiang.” Its bibliography names Brown–Xiang, “Proof of the Sendov conjecture for polynomials of degree at most eight” (1999). Tao's arXiv:2012.04125v2, Introduction immediately before Theorem 1.2, likewise says “specifically for all n < 9.” Sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sendov%27s_conjecture and https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.04125.
findings.suggested_fix: To state the cited low-degree theorem, replace `Set.Icc 2 9` with `Set.Icc 2 8` (equivalently, `Set.Ico 2 9`) and update the docstring to “degree at most 8.” Rename the variant accordingly.

status_issues.source_status: The current source records a full proof posted by Lech Mazur on 5 August 2026, followed by Terence Tao's verification and exposition on 12 August 2026. Tao also reports Lean formalization and resolution for every n ≥ 2.
status_issues.evidence: Wikipedia's paragraph beginning “On 5 August 2026” reports the proof and Tao's verification. Tao's linked exposition states that the argument “resolves both the Sendov conjecture and the Phelps–Rodriguez conjecture in full generality.” URLs: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sendov%27s_conjecture and https://terrytao.wordpress.com/2026/08/12/a-digestion-of-the-proof-of-sendovs-conjecture/.
status_issues.suggested_change: Change the main theorem's category to `research solved` and add the current proof/exposition reference. Keep its mathematical statement unchanged.

reformulations.difference: The nearby-critical-point conclusion is expressed using `Metric.infDist` on distinct root sets, rather than an explicit critical point w with |z − w| ≤ 1.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Under `f.IsSendov`, f has degree at least 2. Over ℂ its derivative has degree f.natDegree − 1 ≥ 1, so its root set is nonempty by the fundamental theorem of algebra. That root set is finite, hence compact, so the infimum distance is attained. Consequently `infDist ≤ 1` is equivalent to an actual root of the derivative within distance 1. Both polynomials are nonzero, so root-set membership is equivalent to evaluation being zero. Root multiplicities do not affect these pointwise conditions. The equivalences, including the evaluation-and-norm formulation, were proved in the scratch file without using the conjecture theorems.

reformulations.difference: The Lean statement allows arbitrary leading coefficients rather than imposing the monic normalization displayed in Wikipedia's product formula.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The degree hypothesis makes the leading coefficient nonzero. Multiplication by its inverse produces a monic polynomial with the same degree and roots. Its derivative is multiplied by the same nonzero constant, so the critical points and their distances are unchanged. Conversely, the arbitrary-polynomial statement immediately specializes to monic polynomials. The degree-wise equivalence with the statement restricted to monic polynomials was proved in the scratch file.

sources_consulted: https://arxiv.org/e-print/2012.04125 (read sendov.tex: abstract, Conjecture 1.1, Theorem 1.2, surrounding discussion, and Brown–Xiang bibliography entry)

Mathlib at the supplied checkout: polynomial roots, degree and derivative definitions; complex root existence; polynomial analytic derivatives; Metric.infDist and compact-set minimizers; Filter.eventually_atTop.
review.notes: Checked all five declarations. /workspace/review/scratch.lean compiles and verifies the reformulations without sorry-backed conjecture dependencies. Boundary tests exclude zero, constant and linear polynomials; X^n supplies admissible polynomials for every n ≥ 2; X² − 1 has critical-point distance exactly 1. The eventual variant is exactly ∃ N, ∀ n ≥ N, n.SatisfiesSendovConjecture, with a uniform threshold, matching Tao's theorem. No additional mathematical defects or status issues were found.

demonstrated.claim: The declared hypothesis admits degree 9, which the cited bound n < 9 excludes, and X^9 satisfies the polynomial hypotheses with actual degree 9.

submission.summary: Created /workspace/review/trivial_proof.lean. It checks the exact imported theorem type using type_of% and demonstrates the off-by-one hypothesis with compiled examples. It neither proves nor refutes Sendov's conjecture and does not use any sorry-backed theorem proof.

trivial_proof.lean:
import FormalConjectures.Wikipedia.Sendov

/-!
The cited Brown–Xiang result covers `2 ≤ n < 9`, not `2 ≤ n ≤ 9`.
These checks exhibit the extra degree in the hypothesis; they do not prove or refute Sendov.
-/

-- Sendov.sendov_conjecture.variants.le_nine: its exact type requires the whole degree-9 case.
example (h : type_of% @Sendov.sendov_conjecture.variants.le_nine) :
    Sendov.Nat.SatisfiesSendovConjecture 9 :=
  h 9 (by decide)

-- Sendov.sendov_conjecture.variants.le_nine: 9 satisfies the declared bound but fails the source's n < 9.
example : (9 : ℕ) ∈ Set.Icc 2 9 ∧ ¬ ((9 : ℕ) < 9) := by
  decide

-- Sendov.sendov_conjecture.variants.le_nine: X^9 is admissible of actual degree 9, so this case is nonvacuous.
example : Sendov.Polynomial.IsSendov (Polynomial.X ^ 9 : Polynomial ℂ) ∧
    (Polynomial.X ^ 9 : Polynomial ℂ).natDegree = 9 := by
  simp [Sendov.Polynomial.IsSendov,
    Polynomial.rootSet_X_pow (S := ℂ) (by decide : 9 ≠ 0)]

submission.summary: Restricted the low-degree variant to `Set.Icc 2 8`, renamed it to `Sendov.sendov_conjecture.variants.le_eight`, and corrected its docstring to say degree at most 8. Other declarations were left unchanged. The prescribed compile command succeeds with only the expected `declaration uses 'sorry'` warnings.
